brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.delete
objective.description: Delete one local matter, remove it from the runtime catalog, and notify local brique subscribers.

#root.role: Resolve one matter identifier, remove its local storage and runtime catalog entry, and emit a deletion acknowledgement.

expected_revision._comment: Optional optimistic guard checked under the matter lock.

deleted._comment: The concrete deleted matter is the one designated by params.matter_id in the current context.

effects.matter_descriptor: The local descriptor and engine-owned substance files are removed through a recoverable deletion journal.
effects.catalog: The local matter catalog entry is removed.
effects.subscriptions: Local brique subscribers may be notified of the deletion.

transformation_contract.morphing: A local matter identifier becomes an explicit deletion of the corresponding matter state from disk, catalog, and local brique subscription visibility.
invariants: matter.delete operates on one local catalog identity only.
Catalog presence is authoritative for deletion eligibility; disk absence alone does not prevent deletion once the catalog entry exists.
Every supplied revision or byte-size guard must match before any removal.
Once the deletion journal is committed, an interruption is rolled forward at startup before the Matter loop accepts work.
success: On success, matter.delete returns ok=true and echoes the deleted matter_id.
Successful deletion removes the matter from the runtime catalog and triggers local brique deletion notifications when local subscriptions existed.
failure: The capacity fails when matter_id is missing.
The capacity refuses deletion when the matter is absent from the runtime catalog.
A failure before the recovery journal is committed leaves the matter untouched; a later failure retains recovery evidence and reports an internal error.
notes: Missing owned files are tolerated, but filesystem errors are not reported as successful deletion.
Deletion is local to the current context.
